workedSteps: For constant net force along displacement, Wnet = ΔK = ½m(v²−u²).
Use m=4 kg, initial speed 3 m/s, final speed 5 m/s: ½×4×(25−9).
Net work is +32 J and the body's kinetic energy increases.
Kinetic energy is given by K=½mv².
For a mass of 3 kg moving at 4 m/s, evaluate ½×3×4².
The answer is 24 J; velocity must be squared.
For motion from rest under constant force, the net work Fd=½mv².
At the same mass and displacement, doubling force doubles work and final kinetic energy.
Therefore v_new²=2v² and v_new=√2 v.
For a linear force–displacement graph use signed trapezoid area ½(F0+F1)d.
Insert (+12 N, −4 N) across 8 m: ½(12−4)×8.
Positive area +36 J minus negative area 4 J gives +32 J.
Graphical work equals the signed area under the parallel-force graph.
The triangle has a 6 m base and 9 N height above the axis.
Thus ½×6×9=+27 J of work.
Use the scalar-product relation W=Fd cosθ.
Here cos120°=−0.5, with F=10 N and d=3 m.
W=10×3×(−0.5)=−15 J, because the forward component is negative.
Gravity is conservative and work depends only on endpoint height difference.
Reversing the endpoints reverses the height difference and hence the work's sign.
Wgravity for B→A is −40 J when A→B gives +40 J.
Near Earth gravitational work is mg(hstart−hend), independent of route length.
Kinetic friction does approximately −fk L, depending on total distance L.
Gravity is conservative, while friction is generally path-dependent.
A conservative force performs equal work on different paths between the same endpoints.
The recorded work differs, +14 J on one route but +9 J on another.
That path dependence establishes a non-conservative force.
Initial kinetic energy is K0=½×3×4²=24 J.
Net work is (5−8)×3=−9 J, so target energy Kf=15 J stays positive.

Initial kinetic energy K0=½×5×4²=40 J.
An opposing force of 10 N removes 10 joules per metre of motion.
Stopping distance is 40 J÷10 N=4.0 m.
Work done BY the resisting force is negative: Wres=−Frd.
Here Wres=−5×2=−10 J; this is the frictional loss.
Work supplied AGAINST resistance is the positive magnitude +10 J.

Wapplied=+30 J; the separate resistive work is not included here.
Resistance does negative work Wres=−FrL along a travelled path.
Changing the path length L generally changes this dissipation for the same endpoints.
